# StraviFX

> StraviFX is an AI chart analysis app for Android. Point your camera at any forex, gold, stock or crypto chart (or pick a live market and timeframe) and it reads the market structure, makes a buy, sell or stand-aside call with a confidence score, and lays out the trade: entry, stop loss, two take-profit targets and a position size. Every setup is saved to a journal and tracked to its outcome. StraviFX is built by Infinytech Solutions in Nairobi, Kenya. It is sometimes written "Stravifx". It is not related to Strava or StriveFX.

StraviFX provides analysis for information and education only. It is not financial advice, it does not place trades, and its confidence score is not a probability of profit.

## Tools

- [Trading calculators hub](https://www.stravifx.app/tools): the three free calculators below, which one to use first, one EUR/USD trade worked through all three, and the lot and pip conventions they share

- [Lot size calculator](https://www.stravifx.app/tools/lot-size-calculator): position size in lots and units from balance, risk % and stop loss in pips, for USD-quoted pairs, USD/JPY and JPY crosses, USD/CAD, USD/CHF and gold (XAU/USD), with the formula and worked examples
- [Pip calculator](https://www.stravifx.app/tools/pip-calculator): pip value per standard, mini and micro lot for majors, JPY pairs, crosses and gold (XAU/USD), in a USD, EUR or GBP account, with the formula and worked examples
- [Risk reward calculator](https://www.stravifx.app/tools/risk-reward-calculator): risk-to-reward ratio and break-even win rate from entry, stop loss and take profit for forex pairs, JPY pairs and gold (XAU/USD), with optional spread and commission, the formulas and worked examples

## Glossary

- [Trading glossary](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary): plain-English definitions of the terms the StraviFX app uses; where traders disagree, each page names the variants and states StraviFX's convention (a level counts as broken only on a candle close)
- [Market structure](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/market-structure): swing highs and lows; bullish (higher highs, higher lows), bearish (lower highs, lower lows) and range; how timeframes change the reading
- [Break of Structure (BOS)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/break-of-structure): a close beyond the last swing high or low in the trend's direction; close vs wick conventions; BOS vs CHoCH
- [Change of Character (CHoCH)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/change-of-character): the first close against the trend (below the last higher low, or above the last lower high); CHoCH vs BOS vs market structure shift (MSS)
- [Market Structure Shift (MSS)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/market-structure-shift): the confirmed flip after a CHoCH (a failed swing in the old direction, then a close beyond the next swing); the three meanings traders give MSS; displacement and liquidity sweeps as optional filters
- [Swing high / swing low](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/swing-high-swing-low): a candle whose high (low) beats its neighbours; 1, 2 and 3-candle rules; why swings confirm late; wicks for swings, closes for breaks
- [Higher highs / higher lows](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/higher-highs-higher-lows): labelling swings HH, HL, LH, LL; which combinations are trends and which are ranges; how an uptrend ends
- [Range / consolidation](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/range-consolidation): price between a ceiling and a floor; marking the edges from wicks; a close outside ends the range; why the middle is the worst entry
- [Retest](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/retest): price returning to a level it just closed beyond; when a retest holds or fails; retest entry vs chasing the break, with stop and lot size compared
- [Liquidity](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/liquidity): market liquidity vs liquidity on a chart (resting stop orders); where it pools; sweep vs break decided by the close; where not to put your stop
- [Liquidity sweep / stop hunt](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/liquidity-sweep): a push past an obvious high or low that triggers the stops there and closes back inside; sweep vs false breakout vs breakout; StraviFX counts a sweep only when the same candle closes back inside
- [Buy-side / sell-side liquidity](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/buy-side-sell-side-liquidity): BSL rests above price, SSL below; why the names point that way; marking both pools; choosing a target from the map
- [Equal highs / equal lows](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/equal-highs-equal-lows): EQH and EQL; how close counts as equal (no standard; a tolerance that scales with the average candle range); equal highs vs a double top
- [Order block (OB)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/order-block): the last opposing candle before a strong move away; body vs wick zones; what makes one valid; mitigated vs failed; entry at the top of the body vs the middle, compared
- [Fair Value Gap (FVG)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/fair-value-gap): a three-candle gap where candle 1's high and candle 3's low don't overlap; marked from wicks; full vs partial fill and the 50% line; FVG vs weekend gap
- [Breaker block](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/breaker-block): a failed order block retested from the other side; breaker vs mitigation block (the liquidity-sweep rule); a worked sell example
- [Mitigation block](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/mitigation-block): a failed order block after a swing that fell short of the previous high or low; mitigation vs breaker block; not the same as a "mitigated" order block; a worked sell example
- [Supply / demand zone](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/supply-demand-zone): the base a sharp move left from; proximal and distal lines; drop-base-rally and rally-base-drop; fresh vs tested zones; a worked gold example
- [Premium / discount](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/premium-discount): a dealing range split at its 50% midpoint (equilibrium); how to pick the range; why a discount entry risks less for the same target, with two entries compared
- [Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/optimal-trade-entry): the 62–79% retracement of the last impulse leg (70.5% as the middle line); 62/79 vs 61.8/78.6; OTE vs the golden pocket; a worked EUR/USD example compared with a 50% entry
- [Entry](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/entry): the price a trade opens at; market, limit and stop entries; why the entry sets risk and reward when the stop and target come from the chart; the bid/ask spread catch; a worked USD/JPY example
- [Stop loss](https://www.stravifx.app/glossary/stop-loss): an order that caps the loss; placed beyond the level that proves the idea wrong plus a buffer, then the lot size follows; stop vs stop-limit vs trailing vs guaranteed; gaps can fill it worse (cites Investor.gov); a worked gold example

## Facts

- Platforms: Android (Google Play)
- Markets: forex, stocks, crypto and gold; timeframes from 5 minutes to 1 week
- Hourly checks: EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, XAU/USD, GBP/JPY, AUD/USD
- Inputs: a photo of a screen, a screenshot, or a live market with no chart needed
- Outputs: trend and structure in plain English, a call with confidence, an execution ladder (entry, stop, TP1, TP2 with pips and reward-to-risk), lot size from account equity and risk percentage, and a journal of outcomes
- Pricing: free to download, with optional subscriptions
- Support: stravifxapp@gmail.com
